chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
He said: The free man is not killed for the slave. And when the free man kills the slave, he is fined its price, and is whipped with a severe whipping.

key_terms.الْحُرُّ: The free man (as opposed to a slave)

ai.seo_question: What is the compensation and punishment for a free man who kills a slave in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of 'diya' (blood money) and 'jabr' (severe corporal punishment) rather than 'qisas' (retribution) when a free man kills a slave, reflecting the socio-legal hierarchy of the time. It highlights the Shia jurisprudential view that while the slave's life has value, the equality required for capital execution is not fully present between the free and the enslaved, a nuance debated by scholars like al-Shaykh al-Mufid and al-Tusi.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The free would not be killed due to the slave. And when the free one kills the slave, he would be fined his value, and would be whipped with intense whipping’.
